title: Rejetto HTTP File Server RCE
rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Rejetto HFS Command Injection CVE-2014-6287
id: 5a3e9d4f-8b2c-4d7a-9e1f-2c8a1b4e6d9f
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of Rejetto HTTP File Server vulnerability (CVE-2014-6287) via unauthenticated HTTP GET request with null byte injection in the search parameter, which triggers command execution.
references:
    - https://vk9-sec.com/hfs-code-execution-cve-2014-6287/
    - https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/39161
    - https://github.com/Twigonometry/Cybersecurity-Notes/blob/c875b0f52df7d2c7a870e75e1f0c2679d417931d/Writeups/Hack%20the%20Box/Boxes/Optimum/10%20-%20Website.md
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-29
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1203
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - '%00{.+exec|'
            - 'search=%00{.+exec|'
        cs-method: GET
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools using similar search patterns
level: high

title: Execution of Command Injection Payload in Rejetto HFS CVE-2014-6287
id: 7b4f0e5a-9c3d-5e8b-0f2a-3d9b2c5f7e8a
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of command injection payloads in Rejetto HTTP File Server (CVE-2014-6287) by monitoring for PowerShell and netcat download/executions in HTTP request parameters.
references:
    - https://vk9-sec.com/hfs-code-execution-cve-2014-6287/
    - https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/39161
    - https://github.com/Twigonometry/Cybersecurity-Notes/blob/c875b0f52df7d2c7a870e75e1f0c2679d417931d/Writeups/Hack%20the%20Box/Boxes/Optimum/10%20-%20Website.md
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-29
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1203
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - 'powershell.exe'
            - 'nc.exe'
            - 'http://.*nc.exe'
            - 'C%3a\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe'
        cs-method: GET
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using PowerShell or netcat
level: high

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Unauthenticated File Upload to SAP NetWeaver Metadata Uploader
id: 079a2ae3-d6b4-478d-8401-ac9764f4cfb3
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2025-31324 in SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer through unauthenticated file upload to /developmentserver/metadatauploader endpoint, leveraging POST requests with binary content type and JSP webshell payloads.
references:
    - https://blog.eclecticiq.com/china-nexus-nation-state-actors-exploit-sap-netweaver-cve-2025-31324-to-target-critical-infrastructures
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-29
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection1:
        cs-method: 'POST'
        cs-uri-query: '/developmentserver/metadatauploader'
        request_header|contains: 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream'
    selection2:
        request_body|contains:
            - 'upload.jsp'
            - 'helper.jsp'
            - 'forwardsap.jsp'
    condition: all of selection*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools uploading files to SAP endpoints
level: high

id: ca7d944a-505b-432a-af4d-0cfdc4808b94

pipeline.attack_summary: China-nexus APTs exploited CVE-2025-31324 in SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer to gain unauthenticated remote code execution. They deployed webshells like coreasp.js and forwardsap.jsp, used KrustyLoader via AWS S3 buckets for second-stage payloads, and leveraged SNOWLIGHT downloader with VShell RAT for persistent access. C2 communication occurred over TCP 10443 and 443 using domains such as sentinelones.com and oastify.com.

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up clearly describes how the initial access was achieved through a phishing email with an ISO attachment containing EarthTime.exe, which then triggers SectopRAT via MSBuild.exe. The attack chain is well-documented and focuses on execution rather than network exploitation.

pipeline.attack_summary: Threat actors gained initial access via a malicious EarthTime.exe file impersonating legitimate software, which deployed SectopRAT malware through MSBuild.exe. They used multiple reconnaissance tools including Grixba (Play ransomware), SharpHound, AdFind, and SoftPerfect NetScan to map the environment. Persistence was established through startup folder shortcuts and local account creation. Privilege escalation occurred via PsExec, while credential access was achieved through DCSync attacks, Veeam database dumping, and Betruger backdoor. Lateral movement was performed using RDP and WMIexec, with exfiltration conducted via WinRAR and WinSCP to a cloud-hosted FTP server.
